name: Young Adult-Onset Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy
aliases: Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy Type II
Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy with Young Adult Onset

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs with onset in young adulthood
Electromyography (EMG) showing chronic denervation and motor axonal neuropathy without sensory involvement
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with distal hereditary motor neuropathy (e.g., HSPB1, GARS)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Absence of significant sensory deficits on clinical and electrophysiological examination

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal motor neuropathy symptoms with supportive electrophysiological findings and either genetic confirmation or consistent family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Sensory nerves are typically spared, distinguishing this condition from other neuropathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness predominantly in lower limbs
searchTerms: weak muscles at lower limb ends

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle atrophy of feet and lower legs
searchTerms: muscle wasting in feet and lower legs
loss of muscle bulk in distal legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of sensory loss despite motor deficits

common.symptomName: Foot drop due to dorsiflexor weakness
searchTerms: foot drop from weak foot dorsiflexors

common.symptomName: Muscle cramps and fasciculations in distal limbs
searchTerms: muscle twitching in hands and feet
muscle spasms in arms and legs

common.symptomName: Mild hand weakness in advanced stages
Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes in affected limbs

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal sensory symptoms such as paresthesias (rarely present)
Gait instability due to distal weakness

searchTerms: signs of upper motor neuron damage
difficulty breathing due to weak respiratory muscles
weakness in muscles that help breathing

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic and inflammatory neuropathies
imaging: Muscle MRI may show selective distal muscle atrophy
Nerve ultrasound may show reduced cross-sectional area of motor nerves
other: Electromyography demonstrating chronic denervation and reinnervation changes
Nerve conduction studies showing reduced motor amplitudes with preserved sensory responses

distinguishingFeatures: Upper and lower motor neuron signs
No sensory involvement but widespread muscle involvement

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness over weeks to months
Presence of sensory loss or neuropathic pain
references: Rossor AM, et al. Distal hereditary motor neuropathies: clinical and genetic features. Nat Rev Neurol. 2012.
Orphanet: Young adult-onset distal hereditary motor neuropathy. ORPHA:314485.
Harding AE. Distal hereditary motor neuropathies. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 1993.
